propositions: The rebar-implement skill's Phase 4d subagent dispatch lacks a specified model tier, causing it to inherit the orchestrator's expensive model instead of using a cheaper tier for cost savings.
The skill provides no guidance on which implementation work is safe to delegate to cheaper models versus when escalation to stronger models is required.

A Model tiering section must document capability-tier abstractions (strong/standard/cheap) with Claude Code and Codex CLI example mappings to remain harness-portable and resilient to model name changes.

Phase 4d must specify a standard-tier default with a cheap-tier-only-for-transcription constraint and include held-out-TDD invariant preservation that keeps test-authoring and validation on strong-tier.
Phase 3 and Phase 4a must include explicit tier annotations directing appropriate work to cheaper/faster models while constraining specification derivation to strong-tier.
A 4e-bis escalation ladder must distinguish normal held-out iteration from model-weakness triggers without introducing hardcoded module-size numbers.
